assertions.interpretation: The scene is set during the period when Wang Dun held the office of Grand General and was stationed at Yuzhang.
Wei Jie fled the chaos, traveling from Luoyang to seek refuge with Wang Dun — this is the event that initiates the scene.
The conversation between Wei Jie and Wang Dun lasted a full day, marking the duration of the scene's central event.
At that time Xie Kun was serving as Chief Clerk (changshi), anchoring the contemporaneous office context of the scene.
Wang Dun's conditional remark about A Ping (Wang Cheng) refers to a past figure; the hypothetical 'if he were present' implies he is no longer alive at scene time.
The annotation quotes that Wang Bi (Fusi) produced golden words in the Central Court (the Western Jin capital), a past precedent from the Zhengshi era.
The annotation contrasts the past (Wang Bi in the Central Court) with the present ('now') — Wei Jie now resounds in the Jiangbiao region, marking the current scene time.
The annotation records that Wang Dun and Wei Jie discussed for a full day and stayed overnight, extending the scene's duration beyond a single day.
The annotation's quoted phrase describes the thread of the Zhengshi tradition as having been severed and then renewed — a temporal framing of the tradition's continuity across eras.
The annotation notes that Wei Jie arrived at Wuchang, a stage in his journey that precedes or accompanies the meeting with Wang Dun.
